How it works
Four steps from need to confirmed receipt
Every handoff is authorized, timestamped and visible to the people who need to act next — never a separate copy of the data.
Request blood
Requestor or hospital submits group, component, units, urgency and a prescription if available.
Verify request
Authorized Red Cross staff review the request and uploaded document, then approve or reject with a reason.
Find suitable availability
The rules engine ranks compatible verified batches and eligible nearby donors with transparent reasons.
Coordinate fulfilment
Stock is reserved, dispatched and received against the same ledger; the requestor sees each status change.

One platform for the whole coordination chain

AI assists. Rules decide.
Clinical safety first. Genuine ML where it helps.
Compatibility, release status, expiry and protected reserve are deterministic rules — never a model. On top of that, LifeLink evaluates Python XGBoost demand forecasts with a chronological holdout and rolling-average baseline, plus consented donor-response ranking that never decides eligibility.

What this search does not show
It never shows patient identity, prescriptions, donor phone numbers, donor addresses or real-time guaranteed stock. Compatibility is advisory; the treating hospital and blood bank confirm final issue.
Need a compatible alternative?
A+ patients may receive O−/O+ red cells in specific clinical situations, while plasma follows donor-antibody rules (AB plasma is the universal plasma donor). Authorized staff use the rules-based matching panel on each request; do not self-allocate based on group labels.
